S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
examples: Talks incessantly and cannot tolerate silence, continuing to chatter.
Continues to talk even when others are bored or try to cut the conversation short.
Talks too much inappropriately for the situation, making people around them uncomfortable.
Monopolizes the conversation and gives almost no chance for others to speak.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation, is a neurodevelopmental condition marked by persistent, impairing patterns of motor restlessness, excessive talking, difficulty remaining seated or quiet, and impulsive interruption across settings. In adults, it may be partially compensated for by structured routines or activity-heavy work until a life change exposes the impairment; it is distinguished from mania, anxiety, or situational stress by its non-episodic course, longstanding pattern, and absence of a primary mood or fear syndrome.

patient.stressor_event: Gaining a new family member (e.g., birth, adoption, older adult moving in)
patient.stressor: Marco and his spouse took in an older Peruvian relative who needed daily support, turning their lively Tampa home into a multigenerational household just as Marco was leading a district arts-inclusion initiative and taking administration coursework. Over the following 8 months, the loss of predictable decompression time made his long-familiar high-energy style clinically impairing across home, school, and community settings: he could not stay seated through IEP meetings, repeatedly wandered during trainings, talked over colleagues and parents, and intruded into conversations he meant to support. The same driven, animated presence that had once made his classroom engaging began disrupting formal meetings, dinner gatherings, and caregiving routines, leading to complaints from administrators and escalating conflict at home. After a tense school review placed him on a corrective plan, Marco accepted a referral through the district employee-assistance program for psychiatric evaluation.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
S010.manifestation: In IEP meetings or my admin classes, my leg is bouncing under the table, I’m clicking a pen or shifting in the chair so much that people glance over before I even realize I’m doing it.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
S011.manifestation: When I’m supposed to sit through a training, dinner with the family, or a school meeting, I keep finding reasons to get up—refill water, check the copier, look in on my relative—even when I know it makes me look disrespectful.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: Quiet time at home has become almost impossible for me, because if my spouse is trying to watch a show or my relative is resting, I’ll start narrating what I’m doing, humming, or moving things around until someone asks me to please settle down.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: What brings me in is that I feel like I’m constantly running on a motor lately, like I finish one thing at school or home and immediately jump into the next without ever being able to shut myself off.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
S015.manifestation: I’ll go into a parent conference or a staff meeting meaning to be brief, and then I hear myself giving three examples, a story from my classroom, and ideas nobody asked for while the other person is clearly trying to wrap it up.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
S018.manifestation: I keep jumping into conversations between colleagues, parents, or my spouse and our relative because I think I’m helping, but I end up talking over them or taking charge before they’ve even had a chance to finish.

add_requirements.onset_prior_to_age_12_years: My mother used to joke that even in elementary school I taught the class from my seat because I was always out of my chair, talking, or cutting in before the teacher finished directions. This was part of who I was long before adulthood, not something that just started with this family change.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: At work, the complaints have gotten serious enough that I was put on a corrective plan, and at home my spouse says caregiving routines are harder because people have to manage my energy on top of everything else. I feel like I’m damaging trust with colleagues and family even though I’m trying to help.
add_requirements.duration: This level of trouble has been going on for about 8 months, since our older relative moved in with us.
